business_scope.primary_industry_name: Global Export Distribution of High-Proof Traditional Sorghum Baijiu

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Spain (Central State, single-notarial-system jurisdiction, no sub-state tax autonomy for corporate registry)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (unitary national legal system governed by Capital Companies Act and Mercantile Registry Regulations)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Bilateral Investment Treaty between the Kingdom of Spain and the People's Republic of China (signed 14 February 2005, entered into force; includes fair and equitable treatment, no-expropriation-without-compensation and free transfer of funds provisions).

Convention between the Kingdom of Spain and the People's Republic of China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation with Respect to Taxes on Income and on Capital (signed 1990, entered into force 1992; provides permanent establishment taxation, withholding-tax ceilings and exchange of information).

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo, as amended; Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo, Reglamento de la Ley 10/2010; Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, Ley de Sociedades de Capital (articles 25-37 on SL formation and registered office); Real Decreto 165/2019, de 22 de marzo, and Law 5/2018, de 17 de abril, establishing the Registro de Titulares Reales; Order JUS/268/2019, de 5 de marzo, on the UBO electronic register; Directive (EU) 2015/849 (4AMLD) and Directive 2018/843 (5AMLD) transposition.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificado negativa de denominación social (negative company name clearance certificate from Registro Mercantil Central)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: No apostille required for domestic use; issued directly by RMC with electronic signature

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Escritura pública de constitución with draft Articles of Association (estatutos sociales) and appointment of incorporator/director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Spanish notary (Notaría) in the registered-office province
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization only; no apostille when the deed is filed directly in the Mercantile Registry; if later translated for Chinese authorities it will require Hague Apostille by MFA Spain

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized and apostilled Power of Attorney from each Chinese shareholder/director to the Spanish notary / incorporation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Chinese notary office + Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Apostille Service)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing / extract of the corporate register and legal representative incumbency for any Chinese corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) / enterprise registration authority, P.R. China; apostilled by Chinese MFA
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (China is a Contracting Party since 7 November 2023); no consular legalization required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified and apostilled copy of the passport and proof of address of each UBO/shareholder (if resident outside Spain)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Chinese notary public; Spanish consular post if origin is not a Hague Convention party
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for China-origin documents; otherwise consular legalization at the Spanish Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Declaración de titular real (UBO declaration) identifying direct and indirect owners above 25% and senior management in default
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Spanish notary and the future SL's compliance officer / legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized declaration included in the public deed or executed as a separate notarial act; no apostille for Spanish-registry filing

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all shareholders, directors and UBOs against: (i) EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, (ii) UN Security Council sanctions (Terrorism and Non-Proliferation), (iii) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) and Sectoral Sanctions Identifications because USD SWIFT wires and documentary L/Cs will be used, and (iv) Spanish domestic sanctions/PEP registry and BOE official resolutions. Screening must be refreshed within 48 hours before notarial execution and before any name-clearance filing; results must be evidenced in an AML/CFT file and retained for 10 years under Law 10/2010.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC) electronic application: https://www.rmc.es/DenominacionesSociales or via the Sede Electrónica of the Ministry of Justice (portal 'Denominación Social').
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be written in Spanish or in a Spanish-comprehensible form; foreign terms are allowed only as express, expanded trademark/denominative elements. Chinese transliteration in Pinyin is accepted when accompanied by a Spanish generic descriptor (e.g. 'BAIJIU BEBIDAS Y LICORES, S.L.'). All notarial books, deed annexes and registry filings must be in Spanish; any document originally in Chinese must be translated by a sworn-certified translator (intérprete jurado) for incorporation and AML purposes.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: España / Gobierno de España / Ministerio / Administración / Estado
Banco / Caja / Seguros / Reaseguros / Mutua / AFP
Denominations identical to an existing Spanish company or a reserved foreign name
Terms that are unlawful, offensive, contrary to public order, or misleading as to legal form or regulated liquor activity without the corresponding excise/import-export licence
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The RMC negative certificate is effective for 90 days and may be renewed for a further 90-day term by filing a written re-application before expiry. If the proposed name is rejected, the applicant within one month from notification may file a recurso de alzada with the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública (DGSJFP) of the Ministry of Justice, including an alternative naming order. A remedial request can also be made directly to the RMC requesting reconsideration of the confusing-similarity report. If administrative appeal is exhausted, judicial review lies to the Sala de lo Contencioso-Administrativo of the Audiencia Nacional within two months.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Accepted for the SL's administrative correspondence and management address, provided a physical Spanish registered office exists (an SL must maintain a real address in Spain for notification and legal representation). A pure virtual mailbox without personnel or access to accounting records is not sufficient for the AML/tax registered-office test; however, a serviced office, co-working suite or company-administrated address is accepted by the Mercantile Registry and AEAT when all statutory records are actually available there.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate; estimated 5% in the first 12 months if the entity merely conducts wholesale export without physically holding excise goods in Spain, rising to approximately 15-25% when the SL opens a Spanish bonded warehouse, stocks baijiu inventory, or acquires alcohol under excise-duty suspension. AEAT may perform unannounced on-site checks under Excise Duties Law 38/1992 and Customs Inspection Protocol; AML supervisors and SEPBLAC may also coordinate inspections with the Mercantile Registry if UBO data is incomplete.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Negative name certificate (two denomination search orders before Registro Mercantil Central)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registro Mercantil Central / Ministry of Justice
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official public-fee tariff under the Spanish Registry fee schedule; fixed per denomination search (approx. EUR 26 total for two orders)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial deed of incorporation and standard by-laws (SL, including UBO declaration annexes)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Spanish notary (Notaría) with territorial authority over the registered-office province
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial arancel (official statutory tariff set by Royal Decree 1426/1989) computed on capital and deed extent; typical SL range EUR 450-700

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and sworn translation of Chinese corporate certificate of good standing / SAMR registration extract
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Chinese MFA apostille service; Spanish sworn translator (intérprete jurado) or consular legalization post if applicable
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for Chinese notarial certification + apostille + Spanish sworn translation (EUR 350-650)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and apostille of Chinese shareholder passport and address / UBO identification file, plus sworn translation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Chinese notary public and Ministry of Foreign Affairs; Spanish sworn translator
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for certified civility documents; approximate 4 documents at EUR 70-90 per document

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Power of attorney execution, notarization and apostille (Spanish notary + Chinese apostille chain for POA issued by a Chinese shareholder)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Spanish notary and Chinese MFA Apostille Service
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for POA notarization and apostille (EUR 180-320)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT UBO piercing, PEP and sanctions pre-incorporation due-diligence package (Law 10/2010 file preparation)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External compliance counsel / AML adviser retained by founder; no direct state fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing commercial counsel hourly/transaction fee for Spanish AML and UBO verification dossier (flat EUR 1,000-1,800)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: First-year registered-office service and official legal address for SL notices and AEAT correspondence (virtual serviced office accepted)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Corporate service provider in Madrid/Barcelona/Valencia; contractually charged
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for serviced registered office with physical administrative access, EUR 750-1,200 per year

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation tax/AML compliance opinion, initial BOE/digital UBO register filing and representation before Mercantile Registry (post-notarization filing)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Spanish law firm / tax advisor; registration fee paid to the Mercantile Registry separately
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for SL incorporation legal closure and UBO/Sanctions compliance opinion (EUR 1,200-2,000)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, por el que se aprueba el texto refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital (LSC): Art. 4 (capital mínimo de EUR 3,000 para la SL), Arts. 20 a 22 (escritura pública e inscripción en el Registro Mercantil), Art. 22 bis (constitución telemática), Art. 23 (contenido de la escritura), Arts. 33 y 34 (personalidad jurídica y sociedad en formación), Art. 60 (desembolso del capital); Reglamento del Registro Mercantil aprobado por Real Decreto 1784/1996.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (certificación negativa de denominación); Registro Mercantil Provincial del domicilio social (inscripción registral); intervención obligatoria de Notario; notificación electrónica al BORME (Boletín Oficial del Registro Mercantil).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución otorgada ante notario español e inscripción de la sociedad en la hoja registral (inscripción 1ª) del Registro Mercantil Provincial competente.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Capital social mínimo obligatorio de EUR 3,000, íntegramente suscrito y desembolsado en efectivo antes del otorgamiento de la escritura (LSC Arts. 4, 16 y 60). El desembolso debe acreditarse mediante certificado bancario de depósito en una entidad de crédito española a nombre de la sociedad en constitución. Los socios no residentes pueden ostentar el 100% del capital y realizar el depósito transfiriendo fondos a la cuenta provisional. Existe el régimen excepcional de sociedad limitada de formación sucesiva (Art. 4.2 LSC) que admite capital inicial inferior, con restricciones de reparto y obligación de completar los EUR 3,000 con beneficios; en la práctica, una sociedad exportadora mayorista suscribe EUR 3,000 en efectivo.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The founding shareholders, having subscribed the full share capital of EUR 3,000 deposited in the corporate escrow account, approve: (1) adoption of the corporate name and establishment of the registered office; (2) appointment of the Sole Administrator, granting the broadest powers to execute all incorporation and licensing formalities before the Mercantile Registry, Tax Agency, Customs and municipal authorities; (3) ratification of all actions performed in the name of the company prior to registration; (4) opening of bank accounts in Spain; (5) filing of provisional and definitive tax identification applications; and (6) initiation of the municipal opening license, sanitary registration (RGSEAA), and excise warehouse procedures.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certification of corporate name (Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (Madrid) through notary telematic channel or direct online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File an application for a negative name certificate proposing the preferred SL corporate name and at least two alternative names in order of preference. The certificate verifies that no identical or confusingly similar name is registered in Spain and is valid for three months, non-renewable. The notary usually performs this filing electronically before deed drafting. Once obtained, the certificate must be presented to the notary at execution.
required_dossiers: Application form for certification negativa signed by all founding shareholders
Copy of national identity document or NIE of each shareholder
Notarized power of attorney if submitted by proxy
Proof of payment of official fee (approx. EUR 14)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected as identical or confusingly similar, immediately resubmit with the next alternative name; an administrative appeal may be filed with the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública within two months of the rejection notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the incorporation escrow account and deposit of share capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish credit institution selected by the founding shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary corporate account in the name of the proposed company followed by 'en constitución' and deposit the minimum capital of EUR 3,000. The bank issues a certificate of deposit (certificado de ingreso) indicating the account holder, IBAN, amount, and deposit date; this certificate is delivered to the notary. Non-resident shareholders must first obtain their NIE and complete the bank's Know-Your-Customer and anti-money-laundering beneficial ownership declarations.
required_dossiers: NIE certificates and passports of all shareholders
Bank account opening application with AML declarations
Copy of the negative name certificate
Certificate of deposit of share capital issued by the bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines the opening under internal AML scoring for a standard-risk wholesale exporter, resubmit with full corporate background, the negative name certificate, and NIE documentation; because banks exercise commercial discretion, the applicant may alternatively open the account at another credit institution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the notarial public deed of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary (Notario) within the territorial district of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Spanish attorney to draft the bylaws and assemble the pre-incorporation package. All founding shareholders, in person or by notarized proxy, must appear before the notary to execute the public deed. The deed must contain the shareholders' identity, the negative name certificate, the certificate of deposit, the corporate purpose, the registered office, the capital and shares allocation, and the bylaws of the administration organ (LSC Art. 23). The notary verifies legal capacity, reads the deed, obtains consent, and authorizes it.
required_dossiers: Original negative name certificate (valid within 3 months)
Bank certificate of deposit of EUR 3,000
Draft bylaws and deed text
Valid passport and NIE of each shareholder
Corporate resolutions and notarized powers of attorney if a legal entity is a shareholder
Powers of attorney for proxy attendance if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies defects in the draft deed or deficiencies in the shareholders' documentation, correct the bylaws or provide the missing documents and reschedule execution; no formal appeal is necessary as the correction is procedural.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of deeds tax (AJD) and application for provisional tax identification code (NIF provisional)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) and regional tax office of the Autonomous Community
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary submits the deed to the Autonomous Community's tax office for settlement of Actos Jurídicos Documentados, Modalidad Operaciones Societarias, using Modelo 600; in regions applying 'fiscalidad cero' for SME incorporation the quota may be zero. Immediately upon execution, the notary or the company applies electronically for the provisional NIF (Código de Identificación Fiscal) with Form 036 before the AEAT. The provisional NIF is valid for six months and must be replaced by the definitive NIF after registration.
required_dossiers: First copy of the notarial deed
Modelo 600 self-assessment for AJD (or tax exemption certificate where applicable)
Form 036 census declaration including CNAE activity code
Identities (NIE/passport) of shareholders and the appointed administrator
Power of attorney of the legal representative filing the NIF application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEAT queries the NIF application for inconsistency between the stated corporate purpose and the requested CNAE classification, rectify the census declaration and resubmit; if the provisional NIF is not issued, the company may file a further electronic application after the AJD payment certificate is uploaded.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription in the Provincial Mercantile Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial of the province of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the petition of registration with the Provincial Mercantile Registry within two months of the notarial execution, attaching the notarized deed, the provisional NIF, and the payment receipt of the registry fee. The registrar examines legality of the deed and bylaws; upon approval, the first registry entry is made and the company acquires full legal personality (LSC Art. 33). The registry fee tariff is based on the capital amount, approximately EUR 120 for a EUR 3,000 capital.
required_dossiers: Original public deed together with a testimonially-issued copy
Petition for registration signed by the administrator
Copy of provisional NIF
Proof of payment of the registry tariff
Modelo 600 payment record if not already stamped
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a defect note, correct the identified irregularity and resubmit within 60 days; if the registrar remains silent for more than 15 days, the company may request accelerated action ('desistimiento') or file an appeal before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública against the denial or inactivity.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining definitive NIF, BORME publication, and registry certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); Registro Mercantil Provincial; BORME publication office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the inscription, obtain a certificate of registration (certificación de la hoja registral) from the Mercantile Registry. File Form 036 as a census modification to exchange the provisional NIF for the definitive NIF, submitting the registry certificate. The Mercantile Registry publishes the incorporation entry in the BORME official gazette; the publication fee is included in the registration proceedings.
required_dossiers: Certificate of registration issued by the Provincial Mercantile Registry
Provisional NIF certificate
Form 036 modification filing
Registry fee receipt evidencing BORME publication inclusion
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the provisional NIF expires before issuance of the definitive NIF, apply for a new provisional NIF using the registration certificate and an explanatory letter to the AEAT; if the BORME announcement is delayed, the registry provides a publication certificate upon request.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Census registration of the economic activity (CNAE 4634 and IAE epigraph 613)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), provincial tax office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the final census declaration in Form 036 declaring the start of operations under CNAE 4634 'Comercio al por mayor de bebidas' (equivalent to ISIC 4632) and IAE epigraph 613 'Comercio al por mayor de productos alimenticios, bebidas y tabaco'. Even though companies with annual turnover below EUR 1 million are exempt from the IAE quota, the census registration itself is mandatory and must be completed before invoicing. Attach the rental title and the definitive NIF.
required_dossiers: Form 036 definitive census declaration
Definitive NIF certificate
Mercantile Registry registration certificate
Lease agreement or title of the registered office premises
Municipal activity license reference if already issued
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEAT or the municipality disputes the premises category or the start date, submit the lease contract, the registration certificate, and any preliminary occupation license to obtain a rectified census record; appeals follow the AEAT telematic claims procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Sanitary registration as food business operator (RGSEAA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Española de Seguridad Alimentaria y Nutrición (AESAN) and the regional Consejería de Sanidad where the registered office is located
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before the first storage or distribution of the Chinese baijiu, register the company in the Registro General Sanitario de Empresas Alimentarias y Alimentos (RGSEAA) under the activity 'wholesale trade of alcoholic beverages, including warehousing'. The application includes the company data, the list of food activities, and a declaration that the storage premises comply with food safety requirements. The alcohol beverage product labels must separately comply with Regulation (EU) 1169/2011 for the EU market and with destination-country labeling rules for exports.
required_dossiers: RGSEAA registration application of the food business operator
Definitive NIF and Mercantile Registry certificate
Municipal activity license or declaration responsible
Description of the warehousing and storage process for bottled spirits
HACCP-based food safety plan for ambient-temperature storage
Food safety responsible-person declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AESAN or regional sanitary authority returns the application with observations, submit an approved HACCP manual and premises hygiene protocol prepared by a qualified food-safety consultant within 10 business days; reappeal the rejection before the regional health administration if it is confirmed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Excise duties registration, EORI, and customs operator file
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Departamento de Aduanas e Impuestos Especiales de la Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: As a wholesaler and exporter of high-proof spirits, register in the excise duties administrative records as an authorized warehousekeeper or registered consignor of alcoholic products under Ley 38/1992 de Impuestos Especiales and its implementing regulation (R.D. 1165/1995). Apply for an EORI number for customs declarations and register as an intra-community or third-country exporter in the customs electronic systems. If the activity involves exporting goods under suspension of excise duty, provide the customs office with the required bank guarantee document. The company must maintain the legally required stock and dispatch records for alcoholic products.
required_dossiers: EORI number application (Form with AEAT customs office)
Excise registration form for establishments (REA) and operator records
Application for export activity in the electronic excise management system
Bank guarantee certificate for duty-suspension operations, if applicable
Corporate registry documentation and NIF
Description of the premises identified as excise warehouse
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the customs office requires a financial guarantee for duty-suspension movements under the excise regulations, submit a bank guarantee issued by a Spanish credit institution; operations may begin under provisional authorization once the guarantee is lodged and the registration is accepted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal opening license and occupational safety clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ayuntamiento del municipio of the registered office through the Ventanilla Única Empresa (VUE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the municipal application for the activity license of the administrative office and the bonded warehouse. Most major municipalities require a communication or declaration responsable for small-scale wholesale premises with a fire-prevention certificate; certain premises require the full licensing procedure and prior building inspection by municipal technicians. The application includes plans, the activity report, the fire safety certificate, and the occupational risk prevention plan (Ley 31/1995 de PRL) approved by a certified prevention service.
required_dossiers: Municipal application form for opening license (licencia de apertura) or declaración responsable
Plans and descriptive report of the premises
Fire protection installation certificate by authorized technician under R.D. 2267/2004
Copy of the lease or ownership title of the premises
Activity report (memoria de actividad) under CNAE 4634
Occupational risk prevention plan and organizational declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal technicians require supplementary measures for fire safety or capacity, present the corrected technical project and the renewed municipal application within 15 days; if the license is expressly denied, file the corresponding administrative appeal (recurso de alzada) before the municipal council within one month of notification.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Consejería de Industria de la Comunidad Autónoma and Ayuntamiento del municipio through the Ventanilla Única Empresa (VUE); technical verifications by authorized industrial technicians
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia de Apertura y Funcionamiento de Actividad Económica (or Comunicación Ambiental Previa / Declaración Responsable, depending on the municipal ordinance and the size of the warehouse)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Consejería de Medio Ambiente de la Comunidad Autónoma; Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico (MITECO) for cross-regional matters
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: No full environmental impact assessment is required for a wholesale spirits warehouse and office activity below the Annex II thresholds of Ley 21/2013 de evaluación ambiental. The establishment qualifies as a municipal environmental communication (comunicación ambiental previa) or a simplified environmental-registration proceeding, unless the warehousing of bulk alcohols exceeds the storage thresholds set by the regional environmental catalogue, in which case a simplified environmental assessment (evaluación ambiental simplificada) is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges to the municipal sewer must comply with R.D. 1620/2007 and the municipal ordinance limits, typically BOD5 not exceeding 300 mg/L, COD not exceeding 500 mg/L, and pH between 6 and 9; no industrial process wastewater is generated in dry warehousing. Volatile organic compound emissions from ethanol evaporation must remain below the 2 tonnes-per-year threshold; if exceeded, the installation falls under the regional air-emission authorization consistent with Directive 2010/75/EU. Packaging waste (glass, PET, cardboard) must be managed under a packaging waste minimization plan per Ley 11/1997 and R.D. 1055/2013, with records filed in the electronic waste-tracking system (e-DAE). Spill prevention requires secondary containment of pallets, drip trays, and absorbent materials for alcohol releases.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate (Certificado del instalador autorizado in accordance with R.D. 2267/2004 Reglamento de Seguridad contra Incendios) certifying the installation of portable extinguishers at a maximum coverage of 200 m² each, emergency lighting, signage, and evacuation routes; structural load certificate for the pallet racking system; occupational risk prevention program under Ley 31/1995 de Prevención de Riesgos Laborales including a written risk assessment, emergency and evacuation plan, and the engagement of a certified external prevention service; labor inspectorate clearance may be required before the commencement of operations when the workforce equals or exceeds six employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) — Sede Electrónica: https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Spanish SL is formed by notarial deed and registration in the Mercantile Registry. The SL must then submit Form 036/037 (Censo de Empresarios, Profesionales y Retenedores) to obtain or confirm its definitive NIF and VAT registration. A foreign non-resident entity acting without a Spanish SL but through a permanent establishment must request a non-resident NIF through Form 036/037 using a tax representative, filing a notarised and apostilled certificate of incorporation, proof of representative authority, and evidence of the Spanish permanent establishment registration. For intra-Community supplies and purchases, the taxpayer must be assigned a NIF-IVA, which is applied for through the same census declaration and must be reflected in VIES records.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (a Spanish SL is a capital entity taxed under the Impuesto sobre Sociedades at the standard 25% rate; it is resident and taxed on worldwide income. Territorial rules apply only to non-resident entities without a permanent establishment, and Tax_Exempt_Zone treatment is limited to qualifying entities in the Canary Islands ZEC regime.)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain does not operate a US-style check-the-box regime. Available statutory elections include the group tax consolidation regime for Spanish-based groups with at least 75% direct or indirect voting control, the VAT group (Grupo IVA) regime, options on depreciation and asset amortisation methods, and the simplified VAT regime for small business where turnover and purchases are each below EUR 250,000. Hybrid mismatch rules implementing ATAD apply and prevent elective arbitrage through dual classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA — Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido (VAT/GST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: There is no general turnover threshold for ordinary VAT registration: any legal person performing taxable economic activity in Spain must register before commencing activity. The simplified IVA regime is available only to small traders with annual turnover not exceeding EUR 250,000 and annual purchases not exceeding EUR 250,000; a wholesale spirits-export trader exceeding those limits, or opting out, must operate under the general IVA regime.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spain mandates electronic invoicing for B2B transactions under Ley 18/2022 (Crea y Crece) and RD 1007/2023. The mandate is phased by turnover: enterprises with annual turnover above EUR 8 million are required in the first phase, all remaining operators in the subsequent phase. Invoicing must be exchanged using a certified electronic invoicing solution guaranteeing authenticity and integrity, commonly in Facturae XML format. Billing software must comply with AEAT 'Verifactu' technical requirements. Large businesses with turnover above EUR 6,010,121.42, or those included in an SII VAT group, must transmit invoice records to AEAT in near real-time under the Suministro Inmediato de Información (SII) using web-service APIs, generally within 8 calendar days for paper documents and 4 calendar days for fully electronic records.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods consigned to a destination outside the EU are exempt with right to a zero rate under Article 21 of the Spanish VAT Law; the exporter must prove that the goods physically left the territory of the European Union within the statutory period and hold transport, customs, and commercial evidence. For a Chinese baijiu wholesale export operation to Latin America through a Spanish SL, zero-rating requires a valid customs export declaration (DUA) and proof of international freight. Intra-Community dispatches to EU customers may likewise be zero-rated if the customer is VIES-registered and the goods are transported to another Member State; EC sales list reporting is mandatory.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA/SAD) with customs documentary
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing shipment to the third-country destination
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT wire/letter-of-credit collection evidence showing receipt of payment from the foreign buyer
Commercial invoice, packing list, and certificate of origin
CMR or alternative transport document for intra-Community dispatches where applicable
e-AD (electronic administrative document) proving excise duty suspension or export release for ethyl alcohol
VAT refund file or formal declaration supporting the zero-rated nature of the supply
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If AEAT determines that the export zero-rating claim was not substantiated, false, or the goods did not depart the EU, the exporter is assessed Spanish VAT at the standard rate of 21% on the invoiced value plus late-payment interest. Tax penalties under Ley General Tributaria articles 191 and 193 range from 50% to 150% of the tax amount involved, with the 150% penalty applicable in cases of concealment or repeated irregular practice. Criminal liability under Article 305 of the Criminal Code may be pursued where defrauded tax exceeds EUR 120,000, exposing corporate representatives to imprisonment and fines. AEAT may retrospectively claw back refunds or VAT credits for up to four years and impose additional excise duty and transfer-pricing penalties when alcohol export or customs evidence is defective.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain) is the Spanish central bank and primary banking supervisor; the European Central Bank (ECB) anchors the Eurosystem monetary framework, TARGET2 real-time gross settlement, and single supervisory mechanism for significant credit institutions. The Dirección General de Comercio Internacional e Inversiones (DGCIIN), part of the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business, administers Spain's foreign investment registry and statistical declaration regime.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible across current and capital accounts, with Spain applying the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union Articles 63-65 on free movement of capital. There are no convertibility restrictions on current-account transactions, trade settlements, or profit remittances. Non-resident profit repatriation is lawful but technically subject to domestic withholding tax (typically 19% on dividends, reduced by the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive or the applicable double tax treaty) and requires evidenciary support of distributable reserves prepared under Spanish GAAP. Capital-account movements are liberalized; however, statistical declarations to the Bank of Spain and the DGCIIN are mandatory for foreign direct investments exceeding EUR 3,000,000 (form D1A/D2A), while lower-value investments and settlements above EUR 50,000 per month must be notified through the bank in the monthly balance-of-payments reporting cycle under Law 19/1993 and Banco de España Circular 1/2011, as amended by Circular 1/2020. The equity injection for the SL falls within a liberalized regime, subject to post-event filing rather than prior administrative authorization, unless the investment triggers sector-specific screening under Royal Decree-Law 7/2021 (e.g., critical infrastructures, dual-use, security, media), which does not apply to an alcoholic beverage wholesaler.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain imposes no mandatory surrender of export proceeds and no required conversion ratio. Eurozone residents may freely retain foreign currency receipts in domestic or offshore accounts. Nevertheless, all export collections must be traceable and supported by customs declarations (Export Control System of the AEAT, with TARIC nomenclature) and commercial invoices. For each transaction or monthly aggregation exceeding EUR 50,000, the settlement must be included in the bank's statistical report to the Bank of Spain. Exporters must retain documentary proof of receipt (SWIFT MT103 advice, bill of lading, customs release) for at least five years to satisfy tax and anti-money-laundering audit requirements.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account + Operational Multi-Currency Account (EUR/USD/CNH)
Operational Account with Trade Finance and Letter of Credit Confirmation Lines
Operational Account for SEPA and EU Settlement
Escrow Account Only for Domestic Iberian Flow

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low-Medium with significant legal constraints. A non-EEA digital e-money institution (e.g., UK-licensed EMIs, Singapore or Hong Kong neobanks) cannot lawfully provide payment accounts to a Spanish SL without obtaining authorization as an Entidad de Dinero Electrónico from Banco de España or passporting an existing EEA license under Directive 2009/110/EC and PSD2. Offshore EMIs lacking a local EUR IBAN and an FGD (Spanish Deposit Guarantee Fund) membership create operational fragility for LC-based trade flows, daily sweeps, and excise duty payments. A domestic Tier-1 bank with UCP600 documentary credit capability is the only recommended primary treasury vehicle. An EEA-passported EMI (e.g., Irish or Lithuanian licensed emitters) may be used solely for small-ticket operating expenses, but should not hold the capital escrow or process supplier settlements above EUR 50,000 due to counterparty risk and the absence of trade finance products.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening is legally permissible under Law 10/2010 provided the credit institution applies enhanced due diligence, including biometric identification and a live video interview with the account signatories and ultimate beneficial owners. In practice, Banco de España-supervised banks insist on at least one physical appearance of the director or an authorized local representative (with a notarized power of attorney) for a non-resident-owned SL operating in a wholesale goods sector. A physical interview at the account-taking branch or at a Spanish consulate reduces onboarding time from 6-10 weeks to 2-4 weeks and materially avoids enhanced due diligence outliers. If remote-only onboarding is attempted, the bank will challenge the corporate resolution, demand an apostilled certificate of good standing from the Chinese shareholder, and require notarized incumbency documentation from the Spanish Registro Mercantil, before the relationship is accepted.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership traceable to the People's Republic of China triggers mandatory enhanced due diligence under EU Directive 2015/849 and Spanish Law 10/2010, especially when the PRC shareholder exhibits a complex group structure or residential address inconsistencies.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A notarized and apostilled UBO declaration (Registro de Titularidades Reales), three years of audited financial statements of each 25%-plus shareholder, a criminal record certificate for each UBO, bank references from a Tier-1 Chinese bank, a legal entity structure chart with percentage interests, and an affidavit accounting for the source of funds used for the capital injection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-proof baijiu classified as alcohol subject to excise duty (Ley 12/2013 and Directive 2020/262) activates sector risk flags, particularly when tax warehouse receipts or Spanish import/export authorizations are missing, or when shipments appear routed to jurisdictions with weak controls.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The AEAT-issued excise import/export authorization, the EU excise movement (e-AD) records, all customs entry summaries and export declarations, certificates of origin (Form A or EUR.1), warehouse receipts from the Spanish bonded warehouse operator, and the complete chain of commercial contracts from the China producer to the Spanish SL and onward to the Latin America buyer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency cross-border wires in USD/CNH with mismatched trade purpose codes are tagged as 'pass-through' or trade-based money-laundering red flags, particularly when invoice value diverges from market benchmarks for distilled spirits.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The full shipment document set (bill of lading, commercial invoice, packing list, insurance certificate), an explicit MT103 purpose-code matrix pre-approved by the bank's compliance desk, a quarterly trade forecast, pricing benchmarks from recognized spirits market indices, and copies of all UCP600 documentary presentations for LC disbursements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Directors or signatories without a substantial physical footprint in Spain are flagged as 'ghost directors,' especially when the registered office is a virtual mailbox rather than a genuine commercial premise.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A Registro Mercantil certificate of incumbency, a genuine Spanish lease agreement for the SL's registered office, the directors' NIE certificates, a Spanish payroll or social security filing demonstrating local substance, and an apostilled board resolution appointing the bank signing authority.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The shareholder's capital contribution must be initiated as a SWIFT MT103 from the non-resident shareholder's bank to the Spanish SL's EUR-denominated IBAN. The wire must reference the Banco de España statistical purpose code for foreign direct investment in equity (code 3001-3002, 'Inversión directa — capital social'), and the beneficiary bank will require a covering memorandum stating 'Apoyo de capital social' and the notarized capital increase resolution. For injections exceeding EUR 3,000,000, the SL must file a post-investment declaration (Modelo D1A) with the Ministry of Economy's Foreign Investment Register within 30 days of the settlement; smaller injections are reported statistically through the bank, monthly. Foreign-currency wires (USD or CNH) must be converted to EUR at the bank's best-execution rate under MiFID II; TARGET2 settlement is used for the final EUR credit. The bank will withhold crediting until the KYC pack, including the RENACEO (Registro de Titularidades Reales) confirmation and the SL's deed of incorporation, is cleared.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound payments include (1) sight/fixed-date SWIFT MT103 for urgent supplier advances and small-value purchases; (2) MT102 for batch supplier settlements within SEPA; and (3) documentary trade settlement via SWIFT MT700 Series (advising, confirmation, amendment) strictly under UCP600, with the Spanish bank confirming the LC for the benefit of the Chinese exporter. The recommended clearing structure for high-value baijiu exports into Latin America is a confirmed irrevocable LC drawn at sight, requiring presentation of a full set of bills of lading, phytosanitary and alcohol content certificates, and the customs export declaration (DEX). Same-day EUR clearing within the EU operates via SEPA Credit Transfer Instant (SCT Inst) with a 10-second cap, while urgent extra-EUR finality is assured by TARGET2 RTGS. For USD settlement, the Spanish bank routes through its US correspondent (e.g., via the Federal Reserve wire network) with a corresponding MT202 cover instruction.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/CNH) with tenors up to 24 months, entered under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with a Spanish bank or EEA-passported bank, subject to EMIR margin obligations, and used to fix export proceeds conversion.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on CNH/CNY, lawfully executed by a Spanish authorized credit institution or an EEA-passported broker and settled in EUR/USD offshore, provided no CNY delivery occurs within Spain; the bank will hedge back-to-back on the international CNH desk.
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD and EUR/CNH) converting USD or CNH trade inflows into EUR for the SL's bond and supplier payment profile, subject to EMIR trade reporting and clearing thresholds.

FX zero-premium collars and participating forwards for the USD leg, permissible for corporates classified as 'eligible counterparties' or 'professional clients' under MiFID II, recommended when annual notional exposure exceeds EUR 5,000,000.

Natural hedging within a multi-currency current account (EUR/USD/CNH balances) is permissible without a separate derivative product, but must be reflected at fair value in the SL's year-end Spanish GAAP financial statements.

EURIBOR-based interest-rate swaps to hedge floating-rate pre-export financing and trade-loan exposure, permissible only when the swap is transacted with the relationship lending bank and documented under the same ISDA schedule.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of annual accounts by shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' meeting of the Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the financial year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure may expose directors to liability and delay filing. It does not automatically trigger strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of annual accounts and management report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry of the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after shareholder approval; for a 31 December year-end, normally by 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry closure may occur if accounts are not filed within one year after the financial year-end. Administrative fines generally range from EUR 1,200 to EUR 60,000, with higher limits for larger companies. Spain has no routine automatic administrative strike-off solely for late accounts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Spanish State Tax Administration Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within the first 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the tax period; for a 31 December year-end, normally 1 to 25 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties, default interest, and possible tax assessment apply. Penalties depend on whether tax is payable and whether the filing is voluntary or requested by the tax authority.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT summary return (Modelo 390), where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally 1 to 30 January following the relevant calendar year; certain taxpayers are exempt because VAT information is reported through periodic returns
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or incorrect filing may result in fixed or percentage-based tax penalties and default interest where tax is underpaid.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership declaration accompanying annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry of the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed with the annual accounts and updated whenever beneficial ownership information changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Incomplete or inaccurate beneficial ownership information may cause filing rejection, registry deficiencies, and potential administrative or anti-money-laundering sanctions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual economic activities tax compliance, where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Spanish State Tax Administration Agency and relevant local authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Applicable only where the company is not exempt, generally because worldwide net turnover is at least EUR 1 million; filing and payment dates depend on the applicable tax and authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment or failure to file may trigger surcharges, default interest, penalties, and collection proceedings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent audit is generally mandatory when the company exceeds at least two of the following thresholds for two consecutive financial years: total assets of EUR 2.85 million, annual net turnover of EUR 5.7 million, or average employees of more than 50. Audit is also mandatory for certain public-interest, regulated, listed, and other legally specified entities.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish General Accounting Plan (Plan General de Contabilidad) and applicable Spanish accounting regulations. IFRS is generally mandatory for consolidated accounts of listed groups and may be used in other permitted circumstances.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: There is no standalone annual UBO confirmation solely for share transfers. The company must maintain current beneficial ownership information, update it after any change in direct or indirect ownership or control, and submit the beneficial ownership declaration with the annual accounts. Share transfers must be recorded in the Register of Members and supported by appropriate evidence.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Register of Directors and their representatives
Minutes Book of shareholders' and management body meetings
Register of contracts between the sole shareholder and the company, if the SL has a sole shareholder

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: EUR 300-1,200 per year, approximately USD 325-1,300, depending on address, mail handling, accounting support, and filing services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: EUR 2,000-8,000, approximately USD 2,200-8,700, where an audit is legally required; no statutory audit fee applies where the company qualifies for the audit exemption

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% general corporate income tax rate. Newly incorporated entities may generally apply a 15% rate during the first profitable tax period and the immediately following period, subject to statutory exclusions and eligibility conditions.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Spain provides tax credits and deductions for qualifying research and development, technological innovation, audiovisual production, certain investments, employment-related measures, and donations. Small entities may qualify for reduced rates where statutory turnover and other conditions are satisfied. Qualifying dividends and capital gains may benefit from the participation exemption, generally subject to a minimum 5% participation and a one-year holding requirement, with additional statutory conditions. Exports of goods outside the European Union are generally VAT-exempt with deduction rights, but this does not exempt corporate profits from corporate income tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200, Corporate Income Tax and Non-Resident Income Tax return for permanent establishments, filed electronically through the Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria, AEAT) electronic headquarters using a digital certificate or other accepted electronic identification.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The return is generally due within the 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the tax year. For a calendar-year taxpayer, the normal filing period is 1 July through 25 July of the following year. If the final day is not a business day, the deadline is extended under the applicable electronic filing rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, Spanish tax identification number, registered address, tax period, legal form, activity classification, accounting period, and filing type.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident company files Modelo 200 only for a Spanish permanent establishment or other taxable Spanish presence subject to the relevant regime. A non-resident without a permanent establishment generally uses Modelo 210 for Spanish-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit or loss per statutory accounts before tax, prepared under Spanish accounting rules or an accepted equivalent basis.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A permanent establishment must attribute income and expenses to the Spanish establishment on an arm's-length basis and maintain records supporting the attribution.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Permanent and temporary book-to-tax adjustments, including non-deductible expenses, depreciation differences, provisions, impairment, finance-cost limitations, related-party adjustments, and exempt income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude income not attributable to the Spanish permanent establishment and document any allocation methodology for shared head-office costs.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax loss carryforwards used in the period, remaining losses, limitation calculations, and applicable continuity and identification information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses must be supported by prior returns, accounting records, and evidence that the taxpayer is entitled to use them. Spain generally permits indefinite carryforward, subject to annual utilization limits and anti-abuse rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base, applicable statutory or preferential rate, gross tax liability, and adjustments for tax credits or incentives.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply only a rate and incentive supported by statutory eligibility. A non-resident permanent establishment must not apply resident-only benefits without satisfying their conditions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Withholdings, payments on account, and installments section
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Creditable Spanish withholdings, prepayments, prior-year installment payments, and final balance payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile Spanish withholding certificates and Modelo 202 payments. Do not claim foreign taxes as Spanish withholdings unless supported by the applicable credit mechanism.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related-party transactions, valuation adjustments, documentation indicators, and, where applicable, information linked to Modelo 232.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report Spanish permanent-establishment transactions with related foreign parties consistently with the local file, master file, accounting records, and treaty profit-attribution principles.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct-debit or electronic payment details, bank reference, return result, authorized filer, and electronic signature.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use an authorized Spanish tax representative or electronic filing intermediary where the foreign taxpayer cannot directly complete electronic filing.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing with no tax payable generally attracts a fixed penalty of EUR 100, or EUR 200 if the taxpayer is formally required to file; voluntary filing without prior notice may qualify for a 50% reduction. Where tax is payable, the surcharge is generally 1% plus an additional 1% for each complete month of delay up to 12 months. After 12 months, the surcharge is generally 15% plus applicable late-payment interest. Formal penalties may apply for incomplete, incorrect, or fraudulent returns, generally ranging from 50% to 150% of the improperly unpaid tax depending on severity.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 202, corporate income tax installment payment return, filed electronically through the AEAT electronic headquarters.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The normal filing windows are 1 to 20 April, 1 to 20 October, and 1 to 20 December. Direct debit normally requires an earlier cutoff. The payment calculation may use either the prior-period tax liability basis or the current-period accounting result basis where the statutory conditions and election apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Spanish tax identification number, legal name, tax period, and payment period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use only for a Spanish corporate taxpayer or permanent establishment subject to Spanish installment payments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Indication of the statutory calculation basis, including prior-year liability or current-year cumulative accounting and tax result.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the method validly selected or mandatorily applicable to the taxpayer and reconcile it to Modelo 200.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Relevant tax base, statutory percentage, deductions or adjustments, and resulting installment amount.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude foreign or head-office amounts not attributable to the Spanish taxpayer or permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount payable, payment reference, direct-debit details, and electronic submission confirmation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Retain the electronic receipt and payment evidence with the corporate tax workpapers.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late payment without prior notice generally triggers graduated surcharges of 1% plus 1% for each complete month of delay up to 12 months, and 15% after 12 months, with late-payment interest after the 12-month point. Failure to file or materially incorrect filing may also produce formal tax penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 232, informative return of related-party transactions and transactions involving tax havens or non-cooperative jurisdictions, filed electronically through the AEAT electronic headquarters when statutory thresholds or reporting conditions are met.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally due during the month following the ten-month period after the end of the tax period. For a calendar-year taxpayer, the normal period is 1 November through 30 November of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Counterparty, tax residence, relationship category, transaction type, amount, and valuation method.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the foreign counterparty's jurisdiction and preserve contracts, invoices, payment records, and transfer-pricing support.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregated transaction categories and statutory threshold tests for reporting.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Aggregate transactions by legally relevant type and related party in accordance with the Spanish reporting rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transactions, holdings, financing, or other dealings falling within the applicable Spanish reporting categories.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Assess the current Spanish list of non-cooperative jurisdictions and apply substance, beneficial-ownership, and anti-abuse documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Responsible person, electronic identification, filing date, and submission receipt.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Spanish entity or permanent establishment remains responsible even where filing is performed by an external adviser.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to provide required information, or providing materially incorrect information, may trigger fixed or proportional penalties under the General Tax Law. Penalty exposure depends on the nature of the omitted data, repeated conduct, and whether the omission affects tax assessment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% Spanish withholding tax on dividends and other profit distributions to non-resident recipients, subject to exemptions and treaty relief. The EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption may apply to qualifying EU or European Economic Area corporate recipients, generally requiring at least a 5% direct participation held for at least one year, subject-to-tax and anti-abuse conditions, and beneficial ownership or equivalent anti-conduit requirements.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Spanish payer generally withholds under domestic law unless it has adequate evidence supporting a lower treaty rate or exemption. Obtain a valid certificate of tax residence issued by the recipient's tax authority, verify beneficial ownership, participation and holding-period conditions, and retain the treaty analysis, corporate documents, payment records, and anti-abuse evidence. File Modelo 216 for non-resident withholdings and Modelo 296 annual information reporting where applicable. Treaty relief is subject to the specific Spain treaty, limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose provisions, domestic anti-abuse rules, and any applicable refund procedure. A refund claim may be filed with the AEAT where excess withholding was applied.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic non-resident withholding is generally 24% for taxable Spanish-source royalties and interest, with a 19% rate generally applicable to residents of EU Member States and certain EEA jurisdictions subject to statutory conditions. Qualifying associated-company interest and royalty payments within the EU may be exempt under the Interest and Royalties Directive, commonly requiring a minimum 25% direct or qualifying group participation, a minimum one-year holding period, subject-to-tax status, beneficial ownership, and anti-abuse compliance. Spain's tax treaties commonly reduce interest and royalty withholding, frequently to rates between 0% and 10%, but the applicable treaty must be checked transaction by transaction.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory documentation is generally triggered where the Spanish taxpayer's aggregate related-party transactions of the same type and under the same valuation method exceed EUR 100,000, or where aggregate related-party transactions exceed EUR 250,000 based on market value during the tax period, subject to statutory exclusions. A master file is generally required for taxpayers forming part of a group, subject to exemptions including the group-size and turnover rules. Country-by-country reporting generally applies to qualifying multinational groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not operate a single standalone Cayman-style Economic Substance Regulation regime applicable to every company. Substance is nevertheless material under the General Tax Law anti-abuse rule, beneficial-ownership principles, treaty principal-purpose and anti-conduit concepts, EU anti-tax-avoidance rules, participation-exemption conditions, interest and royalty exemptions, and permanent-establishment analysis. The SL should maintain real decision-making, appropriate personnel, premises or operational capacity, commercial risk control, accounting records, bank activity, inventory and logistics evidence, and arm's-length pricing proportionate to its baijiu export-distribution functions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and fraudulent corporate income tax reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately concealing sales, fabricating export invoices, diverting customer payments, overstating expenses, or using sham transactions to reduce Spanish taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalties generally range from 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax, depending on concealment, fraud, and severity. Serious tax fraud involving amounts exceeding EUR 120,000 may constitute a criminal offense, with fines commonly linked to the evaded amount and potential imprisonment of one to five years; aggravated cases may carry higher penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers may face joint or subsidiary tax liability, civil restitution, criminal fines, disqualification from management, and imprisonment. Travel restrictions are not automatic and require judicial or enforcement authority; assets may be frozen or seized.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging non-arm's-length royalties, management fees, financing costs, purchasing margins, or commission payments to related foreign entities without commercial substance or supporting documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The AEAT may make a primary transfer-pricing adjustment, impose corporate income tax, late-payment interest, and documentation-related penalties. Failure to provide or correctly provide transfer-pricing documentation can produce fixed penalties per missing or incorrect data point and, where tax is affected, proportional penalties linked to the adjustment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur civil liability for tax damage and, in intentional cases, criminal exposure for tax fraud, accounting falsification, or asset concealment. A group relationship does not automatically protect directors from liability for deliberate misconduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False export, customs, VAT, or excise documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Treating domestic or intra-EU sales as exports, using false customs exit evidence, misclassifying high-proof baijiu, failing to account for import VAT or alcohol excise, or moving excise goods without required electronic movement documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The taxpayer may lose VAT exemption, repay VAT and deductions, and incur VAT, customs, and excise penalties. Goods may be detained or seized, and customs debt, interest, and administrative fines may arise. Repeated or intentional customs fraud may become criminal.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible directors and customs or tax representatives may face joint liability, civil recovery, seizure of assets, professional disqualification, and criminal prosecution where documents are knowingly falsified. Imprisonment is possible for serious fraud; travel restrictions require a judicial order.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Importing, storing, wholesaling, or exporting spirits without required registrations, food and beverage compliance, excise authorizations, traceability, labeling, or warehouse and movement controls.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Authorities may impose excise assessments, penalties, suspension or withdrawal of authorizations, seizure or destruction of non-compliant goods, and restrictions on commercial activity. Serious smuggling or organized excise fraud may result in criminal prosecution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for intentional regulatory breaches, unpaid public charges, and damage caused by unsafe or unlawfully marketed products. Criminal sanctions may include fines and imprisonment in serious cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company, beneficial ownership, and treaty abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Spanish SL as a conduit with no real commercial activity, nominee directors, circular payments, artificial debt, or onward distributions designed solely to obtain treaty or EU withholding exemptions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The AEAT may deny treaty, participation-exemption, interest, or royalty relief, recharacterize transactions, assess withholding and corporate tax, and impose interest and penalties. The tax authority may apply the Spanish anti-abuse rule or the principal-purpose test.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil tax liability, disqualification, asset-preservation measures, and criminal charges where the structure involves fraud, document falsification, or money laundering. Travel bans and imprisonment are possible only under applicable judicial or criminal procedures.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting unexplained cash, payments from unrelated third parties, sanctioned counterparties, opaque offshore accounts, or trade-based money-laundering schemes through invoices, letters of credit, or shipping documents.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Spanish AML authorities may impose substantial administrative fines, publicize sanctions, suspend activities, and require enhanced controls. Money laundering may constitute a criminal offense punishable by imprisonment and fines; sanctions breaches may trigger additional administrative or criminal consequences under applicable EU and Spanish measures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, and beneficial owners may face personal fines, civil confiscation, asset freezing, management disqualification, and imprisonment. Travel restrictions may be imposed by judicial order or under applicable sanctions measures.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining parallel books, recording fictitious inventory or receivables, concealing related-party withdrawals, or disguising dividends and personal expenses as business costs.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Consequences may include tax reassessment, penalties, rejection of deductions, shareholder restitution, insolvency liability, and criminal sanctions for accounting falsification, fraudulent administration, or creditor prejudice.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be required to restore assets, compensate the company and creditors, bear subsidiary tax or insolvency liability, and face disqualification or imprisonment where criminal elements are established.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to retain records and respond to AEAT audits
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Destroying invoices, customs records, bank statements, transfer-pricing files, inventory evidence, customer contracts, or electronic accounting data, or obstructing a tax inspection.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Separate accounting, record-keeping, obstruction, and information-reporting penalties may apply in addition to any tax assessment. The authority may use indirect estimation where reliable records are unavailable.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal penalties for obstruction or deliberate destruction, civil liability for resulting tax loss, and criminal exposure where evidence is concealed or falsified. Imprisonment or travel restrictions require the applicable criminal or judicial process.
